transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Maya Patel (Redwood SE); Jordan Lee (Nimbus, Staff Eng); Priya Rao (Nimbus, CTO); Samir Patel (Nimbus, DevOps)

Summary: quick walkthrough of Redwood SDKs (Python + TypeScript), auth patterns (API key vs SSO), env setup, sample quickstarts, and integration tips. Discussed console usage for keys, Optimize suggestions for batching. Agreed next steps around repos, security docs, and scheduling a POC.

Topics: SDK init, env vars, streaming vs polling, retries/backoff, rate limits, console keys, VPC/private deploy notes, batching/Optimize, example code snippets

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda—i'll do a 10–12 minute demo of the python and typescript quickstarts, Maya will cover auth and console, then we can go into integration q and a.
[00:12] Priya: sounds good, thanks. we just want to see how quick the SDK integration is; our engs are mostly python and node.
[00:24] Alex: perfect. Jordan, Samir—are you the ones who will run the POC?
[00:30] Jordan: yeah i'll lead the eng side, samir will handle infra.
[00:36] Maya: quick note, there might be some slight transcription hiccups, but i'll try to be explicit on the config names.
[00:45] Alex: jumping into python first. we usually set REDWOOD_API_KEY as an env var. example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...; then pip install redwood-sdk, from redwood import Client, client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))—this is the simplest auth flow.
[01:12] Jordan: do you support SSO tokens or service accounts? we can't have long-lived root keys in prod.
[01:20] Maya: yes, we have short-lived service tokens via the console, and for enterprise private you can integrate SSO/SAML and use OIDC-based mTLS for service accounts. also we support KMS-wrapped keys and HSM for private deployments.
[01:38] Priya: great, that aligns with our compliance needs. any audit logs?
[01:45] Maya: full audit trail in Console, per-request logs, and you can stream logs to your SIEM; retention options depend on plan.
[01:55] Alex: switching to typescript demo—npx create-... then yarn add @redwood/inference-sdk (note: transcription might show package name fuzzy), initialize with new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })—typical pattern.
[02:20] Alex: for streaming responses we have client.stream.completions(...) which returns an async iterator; for node you can pipe to SSE or WebSocket in the app.
[02:36] Jordan: how do retries and idempotency work? we have strict at-least-once constraints for some flows.
[02:42] Maya: we recommend idempotency keys on mutating operations; SDK has a header you can set, and retry strategy is exponential backoff with jitter by default. you can override in client config.
[03:05] Samir: mention environment setup: we want to lock down egress, can we restrict IPs?
[03:12] Maya: for Dedicated and Private, yes—dedicated GPU pools can be behind VPC peering and static egress; hosted has regional endpoints and allow-listing for enterprise. we'll follow up with specific IP ranges.
[03:30] Alex: quick note on local dev vs prod: you can run the quickstart locally against hosted with a dev key, but for POC we recommend creating a scoped service token with limited scopes and short TTL.
[03:48] Alex: now live-coding a tiny python example: prompt = "Summarize patient intake notes"; res = client.completions.create(model="rw-instruct-1-small", prompt=prompt, max_tokens=256); print(res.text) — simplistic but shows flow.
[04:20] Priya: what about embeddings? we have search workflows.
[04:25] Maya: embeddings are a separate endpoint, same sdk: client.embeddings.create(...). we also provide batch endpoints and an embeddings cache in Console if you enable Optimize suggestions for caching hot vectors.
[04:44] Jordan: how are costs surfaced? we need token-level breakdowns.
[04:49] Alex: Console shows token usage per route, per model, with cost attribution; you can export csvs or hit the cost API. Optimize will suggest quantization or batching profiles to reduce unit cost.
[05:10] Samir: question on model versions—can we pin versions for consistent latency?
[05:16] Maya: yes, pin model versions in the deployment config or via the SDK by passing modelVersion param, and Console supports rollouts and canary.
[05:30] Jordan: any gotchas with TS types? we've seen mismatched typings in other SDKs.
[05:36] Alex: types are published to npm; for advanced features you might need additional types but we keep them up to date. we recommended pinning @types if you rely on strict linting.
[05:48] Maya: also note the SDK supports both callback and promise styles; streaming types are async iterators.
[06:05] Alex: moving onto auth in Console—showing where keys live, how to create scoped keys with granular scopes (completions:write, embeddings:read), rotating keys, and linking to your SSO.
[06:28] Priya: is there RBAC? we need role separation for dev vs infra.
[06:33] Maya: Console has RBAC, teams, role templates, and you can integrate with your IdP for SSO.
[06:40] Samir: regarding VPC/on-prem—if we go private, how much work is the deployment?
[06:46] Maya: for private we provide an appliance and helm charts; typical timeline is 2–4 weeks depending on compliance and networking. for early POCs Dedicated (reserved capacity) is quicker.
[07:05] Jordan: about quickstarts—can you email the repo and example k8s manifests?
[07:10] Alex: yes will share links; repo includes python/flask and ts/express examples, dockerfiles, and a sample k8s manifest for the hosted integration.
[07:22] Priya: any CI best practices? we need to avoid committing keys.
[07:26] Maya: use secrets manager (aws/azure/gcp) and deploy keys at runtime; we also support short-lived tokens via the console API to avoid long-lived secrets in CI.
[07:45] Samir: rate limits—what are the limits and can they be raised for pilot?
[07:50] Alex: hosted has tiered rate limits; Dedicated gets higher throughput and predictable SLOs. for pilot we'll request higher bursts.
[08:05] Jordan: can Optimize automatically suggest batching sizes?
[08:10] Maya: yes Optimize analyzes traffic patterns and suggests batching configs, cache prefixes, and quantization profiles. it can provide estimated cost savings.
[08:24] Alex: quick demo of Console—showing route-level dashboards, token breakdown, tracing for requests, and the Optimize recommendations tab.
[09:02] Alex: click into quickstart link (shared in chat): github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (note: link may be transcribed imperfectly).
[09:15] Priya: good. are there specific SDK versions tied to runtime features?
[09:21] Maya: mostly backwards compatible; some advanced streaming or kernel features require the newer SDK; we document compatibility matrix.
[09:38] Jordan: how to run local benchmarks? we need to compare latency at 512 tokens.
[09:43] Maya: we can provide a small benchmark harness; for accurate numbers, we recommend running the harness from your infra zone to our regional endpoint or on a Dedicated pool. we also provide sample scripts that generate concurrent clients.
[10:10] Alex: let's open the q & a; Jordan you mentioned idempotency—one more detail: idempotency keys are supported on completion create, and you can set them in the header 'Idempotency-Key'. the SDK helper has idempotency param.
[10:40] Jordan: any advice for embeddings batching? we have daily batch inserts of 50k vectors.
[10:46] Maya: use the batch embeddings endpoint; for very large workloads we suggest chunking and retry policies, and Enable Optimize caching to reduce re-embedding of duplicates. also consider quantization to reduce storage.
[11:05] Priya: security—where are customer data stored, and is PII redaction supported?
[11:12] Maya: for hosted, data residency options by region; audit logs and optional retention/erase policies. PII redaction is a best-effort pre-processing step, we can share recommended patterns and packages. for regulated customers, Private keeps data in your network.
[11:36] Samir: about costs for embeddings storage—do you offer a managed vector DB or is it just embeddings store?
[11:42] Alex: we offer embedding storage as an optional managed store with retention and vector index; some customers bring their own DB—our SDK integrates easily.
[12:00] Priya: ok, timeline: we want a POC in the next 2 weeks ideally. is that realistic?
[12:06] Maya: yes—if you can share network constraints this week, we can have a Dedicated pilot standing in 10–14 days.
[12:18] Alex: recap of next steps and action items — i'll send the quickstarts and sample code; maya will send security docs; samir will provide infra constraints; jordan will confirm stakeholders.
[12:35] Priya: thanks everyone. we'll review and respond.

End transcript.

References shared in chat: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (python, typescript), Console link: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/keys (may be transcribed), Security whitepaper (to be shared).
